A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same relative-KL comparison framework despite retitling and reorganization. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D report original simulation results and DDIM comparisons on CIFAR-10, including confidence intervals for individual image classes.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original simulations and image/text model comparisons. The new confidence intervals are original results, although Table 3 attributes its perplexity values to a public leaderboard.

M1.justification: The empirical mean of log-density differences and normal confidence interval remain unchanged in Equations (5) and (7). Autoregressive likelihoods provide another application of this estimator; the image inversion, Jacobian computation, and learned-inverse procedures are retained.

E1.justification: v2 adds WikiText-2 language evaluation and CelebA face-image evaluation while retaining Gaussian simulations and CIFAR-10. The earlier class-specific CIFAR-10 evaluation in Appendix D is removed. These changes substantially broaden the represented domains and evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds leaderboard perplexity as a reference metric for the GPT-2 comparison. The simulation comparators—kNN KL and empirical W2 with Subsampling or Adaptive HulC—and image FID remain. The added VAE and normalizing-flow models serve as evaluation targets.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce GPT-2 models with 12, 24, 36, and 48 layers, an FP16 variant, and a WikiText-2 protocol treating each non-title, non-empty test line as one observation. VAE/NF configurations and CelebA comparisons are also added. The retained simulation settings and quadratic DDIM schedule are unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 Appendix D/Figure 5 examines DDIM performance separately for cat, dog, ship, and truck images; this analysis is removed. v2 Section 5.3 adds model-size and FP16 comparisons. The learned-inverse robustness check and estimator-bias histograms remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The normal interval construction and simulation reporting over 1,000 repetitions with alpha = 0.1 are retained. Added result tables use the existing confidence-interval practice; no new seed reporting, repeated-run procedure, or uncertainty-estimation method is introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 add VAE/NF, GPT-2, and CelebA results. For example, the new GPT-2 FP16 interval is (-0.008, 0.002), encompassing zero. Retained DDIM values are identical, including the S = 50 interval (-17.40, -16.63), and the simulation plots are unchanged. The four class-specific intervals in v1 Figure 5 disappear.

T1.justification: The formal formulation replaces v1's known-noise and invertible-reverse requirements with accessible sampling density in v2 Assumption 2.2; absolute continuity is retained. The KL-cancellation proposition, unbiasedness result, CLT, and confidence-interval proofs remain substantively unchanged. The image change-of-variables calculation moves to Appendix C.

C1.justification: The central claims of unbiased relative-KL estimation, parametric convergence, and asymptotic inference remain. v2 expands the empirical contribution to image and language models and omits v1's explicit claim to be the first framework providing rigorous generative-model comparison with statistical confidence.

C2.justification: v2 explains the non-significant FP16 comparison through sequence likelihoods and limited test observations, and interprets it as supporting practical use of the quantized model. Section 6 newly identifies conditional generation as outside the current framework. The stochastic-reverse-process limitation remains, relocated to Appendix C.

D1.justification: v2 replaces a generic GitHub profile link with a specific code-repository URL, supplies NF/VAE implementation references and default-training guidance, and documents GPT-2 configurations and WikiText-2 preprocessing. Existing autoencoder training details are retained and moved to Appendix D.1.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 and Table 1 add focused positioning against human ratings and standardized text benchmarks. New citations include Gallifant et al., DeepSeek-V3, FFJORD, and CelebA. Earlier image-evaluation and statistical literature remains, while the blanket first-framework novelty claim is removed.

P1.justification: The title and introduction are revised, and Section 2 is reorganized around problem formulation and accessible-density examples. The main computation section moves into an expanded Appendix C, autoencoder details move to Appendix D, and the appendix gains an overview and clearer subdivisions. This substantially changes the narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds an evaluation-method comparison matrix, a language-results table, and a CelebA table. The original DDIM table becomes a broader model-comparison table, while Figure 5 is removed. Figures 1–4 retain their graphics, with caption refinements and relocation of several displays.

improvement.justification: The clearer density-access formulation, broader image/text experiments, and more precise implementation references improve support for the paper's applicability and make it easier to assess. Removing the class-specific CIFAR-10 analysis sacrifices some evidence about heterogeneous performance. The net gain is useful but limited, with the central estimator and theoretical arguments unchanged.
